body.heading: Friendships fade quietly
paragraphs: Nobody decides to end most friendships. Messages get answered later, then much later, then not at all. Both people feel guilty, and guilt makes reaching out feel even heavier.
The way back is smaller than you think. A friendship does not need a three-hour catch-up to survive; it needs signs of life.

body.heading: Low effort, high signal
paragraphs: Send the photo, the joke, the 'this reminded me of you' message. These take twenty seconds and say the one thing that matters: you still cross my mind.
If you miss someone, say so plainly and suggest something tiny — a call during a drive, coffee next Tuesday. Vague 'we should meet up' plans are where good intentions go to rest.

description: Adult friendships rarely end in arguments — they fade from neglect. Small, regular contact beats grand reunions.
